Every output on this page comes from the package's simulated data. It shows what this step produces and how to read it. It says nothing about any real state: every gap, ratio and rate here comes from how the data were generated.
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(stateELP)
```

```{r}
#| label: run-early
#| include: false
#| ref.label: run-check2
```

```{r}
#| label: numbers
#| include: false
# Values the prose quotes, computed from the results so the text cannot drift
# from the output. Aggregates only.
pct <- function(x) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 0), "%")
num <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")

ct  <- res$crosstab
tb  <- ct[ct$BLOCK == "Total", ]
tot <- stats::setNames(tb$N, tb$COLUMN)
late_n      <- tot[["EXIT_EVER"]] - tot[["EXIT_ONTIME"]]
prolonged_n <- late_n + tot[["NO_EXIT"]]

iep     <- ct[ct$FIELD %in% "IEP", ]
iep_pct <- stats::setNames(iep$PCT, iep$COLUMN)
n_supp  <- sum(ct$SUPPRESSED)

comp <- res$trajectories$composition
ot   <- comp[comp$EXIT_GROUP == "on_time", ]
ot   <- ot[order(ot$YEAR_IN_STATUS), ]
ot_first <- ot$PCT_OF_MEASURED[[1]]
ot_gone  <- min(ot$YEAR_IN_STATUS[ot$PCT_OF_MEASURED %in% 0])

ac       <- res$academic_summary
y_first  <- min(ac$YEAR_IN_STATUS)
ac_first <- ac[ac$YEAR_IN_STATUS == y_first, ]
ac_pct   <- stats::setNames(ac_first$PCT_PROFICIENT, ac_first$EXIT_GROUP)
grade_first <- ac_first$GRADE_MODAL[!is.na(ac_first$GRADE_MODAL)][[1]]

component  <- spec_headline_label(spec)
panel_last <- res$meta$panel[[2]]

# The on-time allowance (one value under the simulated spec's flat rule) and
# the grade a kindergarten entrant is in during that year in status.
on_time_y     <- max(res$flags$ON_TIME_YEARS)
on_time_grade <- if (on_time_y == 1L) "kindergarten" else
  paste("grade", on_time_y - 1L)

# The Initial ELP block's "(not reported)" row: its size, and how many exit.
nr <- ct[ct$BLOCK == "Initial ELP" & ct$ROW == "(not reported)", ]
nr_n <- stats::setNames(nr$N, nr$COLUMN)
```

## What this step answers

Check 2 asks **who exits on time, and who gets stuck?** It takes the entry
cohort from Check 1 and splits it by exit outcome. It then compares the
groups on who they are, on how they did on the state content assessment, and
on the English language proficiency (ELP) levels they posted along the way.

A few terms. An English learner (EL) is a student classified as needing
English language support. ELP is measured each year by the state's ELP test.
The simulated spec declares WIDA ACCESS, and its exit rule reads the
`r component`. A student *exits* when they are reclassified as a former EL. A
*cohort* is every student who entered EL status in the same grade in the same
year.

The stage puts a human face on the "stuck" population. Check 1 asks whether
exit timing is driven by English proficiency, as intended. Check 2 is its
descriptive companion. Suppose prolonged classification goes with a
characteristic such as disability status. Then a change to the exit threshold
alone will not fix it. The change would move some students and leave the ones
held back by something other than their English where they were.

## Sample

::: {.callout-note appearance="default" icon=false}
## Sample

`r res$meta$sample`
:::

In plain terms:

- **One entry cohort, the same one Check 1 analyzes.** Check 2 does not pick
  its own. `run_check2()` takes the row that Check 1's `compute_cohorts()`
  marks as selected: the qualifying kindergarten cohort with the longest
  follow-up. In the simulated data that is `r res$meta$cohort`, with
  `r num(res$meta$cohort_n)` students followed through `r panel_last`.
- **Students already in EL status when the data begin are excluded.** Their
  entry was never observed, so their time in status cannot be measured.
- **Three groups, defined against the years observed.** *On time* means
  exiting within `r res$meta$on_time_text` in status. The package dates an
  exit to the first year a student appears as former and counts that year as
  a year in status, with the entry year as year 1 (the same convention as
  Check 1). So a kindergarten entrant first seen as former in
  `r on_time_grade` exited in year `r on_time_y`, which is on time.
  *Prolonged* means everyone still in view who did not exit on time: late
  exiters plus students not observed to exit by the last year of data.
  *Disappeared* means last seen before the window closed, with no exit
  observed. Their outcome is unknown, so they belong to neither group.
- **Censored is not did-not-exit.** A student whose outcome the data do not
  show is *censored*. That covers the disappeared, and also students still
  classified when the data end: they might exit next year. This is why
  "prolonged" always means "prolonged within the years observed".

This is not the state's whole EL population, and it is not the cross-sectional
sample Checks 3 and 4 use. A kindergarten cohort is also the best case for
exit: students who enter in later grades are not in it.

## Status in the package

**Built.** Every result slot the stage's instruction file names is filled:
the exit flags, the crosstab with all five characteristic blocks, the academic
summary, the trajectories, and the Type-gated blocked-groups check. The stage
report (`inst/templates/check2_flows.qmd`) renders in Word and HTML.

What that means for you:

- You can run the stage end to end on your own data today.
- Several design choices are recorded as `[PROPOSED — CONFIRM]` in
  `internal_docs/NOTES-check2.md`. Examples: characteristics are read in the
  entry year; a zero count is shown as zero, not suppressed; "comparable
  point" means the same year in status. Read them before you report.
- **Not built:** repeating the analysis for later start grades as a view of
  its own, starting grade as a crosstab row block, a logistic regression that
  separates correlated characteristics, and a mobility row (the roster has no
  mobility field). The stage report names the first three as later
  additions.

## Before you start

Check 2 does not need Check 1's results object. `run_check2()` calls Check
1's `compute_cohorts()` itself and takes the cohort it selects. It does need
that cohort to exist: if `compute_cohorts()` selects none, Check 2 has no
sample. Running Check 1 first is still the sensible order, because Check 1's
report tells you how the cohort behaves.

| Input | Used for | If it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| Roster: `STUDENT_ID`, `YEAR`, `GRADE`, `EL_STATUS` | The cohort, exit dating, the flags | Required. With no qualifying cohort every analysis slot is `NULL` and `res$meta$note` says why. |
| Roster: `LEFT_TRUNCATED` | Drops students already in status when the panel opens | Students entering in the panel's first year are treated as left-truncated and dropped. |
| Roster: `HOME_LANGUAGE`, `GENDER`, `FRL` (low-income flag), `IEP` (special education), `SERVICE_MODEL` | The characteristic blocks, read in the entry year | That block (or row) is left out of the crosstab, not shown empty. |
| Roster: `DISTRICT_ID`, plus `policy$district_size_bands` in the spec | The district size block | Block left out. |
| Base table: annual-form scores on the ELP component your spec's analyses run on (the simulated spec's `r component`) | The initial ELP band block; the trajectories | Block left out; `$trajectories` is `NULL`. |
| Academic table | `$academic_summary` | `NULL`. |

From the spec, Check 2 reads `policy$timelines`, `policy$suppression$min_cell`,
`policy$academic_benchmark$proficient_level`, `policy$district_size_bands`,
`elp$bands`, `elp$level_scale`, and `policy$exit$types`. Within
`policy$timelines`, the on-time allowance is `on_time_rule$default_years`. If
that is absent, the package falls back to `essa_timeline_years`, then to
`max_years_to_exit`. A `source` of `"provisional"` marks the timeline
`[DERIVED — VERIFY]` in the Sample statement. If `elp$level_scale$type` is
`"categorical"`, `$trajectories` is `NULL`, because category labels have no
mean.

Two spec settings stop the run rather than degrade it:

- `policy$timelines$initial_elp_source` must be `"first_annual"` (or absent).
  The package derives the initial band only as the first annual score.
- An `on_time_rule` keyed by initial band (`by_initial_band`) needs a
  delivered `INITIAL_ELP` column on the roster. See Pitfalls.

## Run it

One call does the stage. Build the spec and the data bundle once, then pass
both:

```{r}
#| label: run-check2
#| eval: false
spec   <- read_el_spec("00_SIM_EL_Spec")
bundle <- as_el_data(el_long_sim, roster = el_roster_sim,
                     academic = academic_long_sim, spec = spec)
res    <- run_check2(bundle, spec)
```

For your state, point `read_el_spec()` at your spec file and pass your own
three tables to `as_el_data()` (see [Setup](setup.html)). `run_check2()` takes
two optional arguments:

- `start_grade`, default `"K"`. The stage's guidance is written for a
  kindergarten cohort, and later start grades are not built as a view of
  their own. Other grades run, but read the Disappeared column with care. A
  student who finishes grade 12 still classified leaves the data and is
  counted as disappeared. In the simulated data, that is what fills a grade 3
  cohort's Disappeared column.
- `subject`, the academic subject for `$academic_summary`. It defaults to the
  spec's first subject (`r res$meta$academic_subject` here);
  `run_check2(bundle, spec, subject = "Math")` reports the other.

The cohort comes from Check 1's table. `SELECTED` marks the one both stages
use:

```{r}
compute_cohorts(bundle, spec)
res$meta$cohort
```

Under the hood, `run_check2()` chains the stage's exported functions. You can
call them yourself to inspect one piece:

```{r}
#| eval: false
co       <- compute_cohorts(bundle, spec)
cohort   <- co$COHORT_LABEL[co$SELECTED]
flags    <- compute_exit_flags(bundle, spec, cohort)      # one row per student
profile  <- compute_cohort_profile(bundle, spec, flags)   # one row per student
crosstab <- compute_crosstab(flags, spec, profile = profile)
academic <- compute_academic_summary(bundle, spec, flags)
traj     <- compute_trajectories(bundle, spec, flags)
blocked  <- compute_blocked_groups(bundle, spec, flags)   # NULL unless Types 2-6
```

## What you get

```{r}
names(res)
```

### `$flags` and `$profile`: one row per student

These two slots hold student-level rows. **Do not print them, and do not
share them.** Look at their size and columns, or at counts built from them:

```{r}
nrow(res$flags)
names(res$flags)
colSums(res$flags[c("EXIT_EVER", "EXIT_MAX", "EXIT_ONTIME",
                    "NO_EXIT", "DISAPPEARED", "PROLONGED")])
table(res$flags$EXIT_GROUP)
names(res$profile)
```

The indicators come from shared helpers (`build_student_spans()` and
`add_exit_flags()`), so Check 1 and Check 2 date exits the same way:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `EXIT_EVER` | Exited at any point in the years observed. |
| `EXIT_MAX` | Exited within the maximum timeline (`policy$timelines$max_years_to_exit`, `r res$meta$max_years` years here). |
| `EXIT_ONTIME` | Exited within the student's on-time timeline (`ON_TIME_YEARS`, from `on_time_rule`). |
| `NO_EXIT` | Still classified in the last year of data. |
| `DISAPPEARED` | Left the data before the window closed, with no exit observed. |
| `ON_TIME` / `PROLONGED` | The split: `PROLONGED` is late exiters plus `NO_EXIT`. |
| `EXIT_GROUP` | `on_time`, `prolonged` or `disappeared`: one value per student. |

The first three are nested: every on-time exiter is also a maximum-timeline
exiter and an ever-exiter. What adds up is `EXIT_EVER` + `NO_EXIT` +
`DISAPPEARED`, which equals the cohort.

`$profile` holds each student's characteristics **in the entry year**. Two
are derived, not delivered. `DISTRICT_SIZE_BAND` bands the entry-year
district by its own current-EL count, using the spec's bands. The package
never uses a delivered district-size column. `ELP_BAND` is the first annual
`r component` level on record, banded the same way Check 1 bands it. For most
students that score is from the entry year; for a student untested that year
it is the first later one.

### `$crosstab`: the cohort split by exit outcome

This is the stage's main table. The display helper shows it as the stage
report does:

```{r}
ft_check2_crosstab(res)
```

The six columns are All, then the five indicators. The report's headers use
the familiar spellings (Exit_Ever, Exit_Max, Exit_OnTime, No_Exit,
Disappeared), and the slot uses the ALL-CAPS codes. The first two rows give
the count in each column and its share of the cohort. Every block below them
is **column percentages**: within one column, they show what that group is
made of.

In the slot, the table is long, one row per block × row × column:

```{r}
names(res$crosstab)
res$crosstab |>
  dplyr::filter(FIELD %in% "IEP") |>
  dplyr::select(ROW, COLUMN, N, N_BASE, PCT)
```

- `BLOCK_TYPE` says how a block's rows relate. `"distribution"` rows split
  the column, so they sum to 100%. A `(not reported)` row keeps that true.
  `"indicator"` rows (Male, Low SES, Special education) are separate shares
  that sum to nothing. A student can count in all three or none.
- `N_BASE` is the denominator behind each `PCT`. For a distribution block it
  is the column total. For an indicator row it is the students in that column
  whose value was reported: an unreported value leaves the denominator rather
  than counting as "no".
- `FIELD` names the roster column a row came from. `ROW` keeps your
  delivery's own codes (for example `spa`). Readable labels are added only at
  display time, from `inst/lookups/Display_Labels.R`.
- `SUPPRESSED` marks cells under the spec's `min_cell`
  (`r spec_min_cell(spec)` here). A suppressed cell has `N` and `PCT` set to
  `NA` and the row is kept. The display shows a dash. A **zero** is shown as
  zero, because an empty cell is not a small cell.
- A dash also appears down a column that no student landed in, because there
  is nobody to describe. That dash is not suppression. The column's count in
  the first row says it is empty, and `SUPPRESSED` is `FALSE` there.
- In the Initial ELP block, `(not reported)` holds students with no annual
  `r component` score on record. In the simulated data these are students
  who took only the alternate form, and students whose composite was never
  reported because a domain was waived. Exit_Ever counts
  `r nr_n[["EXIT_EVER"]]` of these `r num(nr_n[["ALL"]])` students, so the
  row piles up under No_Exit. The generator lets only annual-form students with a composite
  score exit (`sim_contract.md` §3.3). That is a modeling limit, not a
  finding. In your data, check how your exit rule treats these students
  before you read the row.

```{r}
res$crosstab |>
  dplyr::filter(SUPPRESSED) |>
  dplyr::select(BLOCK, ROW, COLUMN, N, PCT)
```

In this run `r n_supp` cells are suppressed: small home-language groups in the
`NO_EXIT` column, and the top initial bands, which are near-empty in a
kindergarten cohort. The Disappeared column is empty (count 0, dashes below)
because the simulated data have no student mobility (`sim_contract.md` §3.2).
Expect a real Disappeared column in your own data.

### `$academic_summary`: achievement at the same year in status

How did on-time and prolonged students do on the content assessment at the
same point in their own trajectories? The comparison point is the same **year
in status** (year 1 is the entry year), not the same calendar year.

> `r check2_academic_note(res)`

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Share at or above the proficiency cut, by exit group and year in status (simulated data). A group with nobody left to test has no point."
plot_academic_summary(res$academic_summary, spec)
```

```{r}
ft_check2_academic(res)
```

The slot's columns are `EXIT_GROUP`, `YEAR_IN_STATUS`, `GRADE_MODAL` (the
most common grade among those students), `N`, `N_SCORED`, `PCT_PROFICIENT`,
`MEDIAN_SCALE` and `SUPPRESSED`. Proficient means
`ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL` at or above `policy$academic_benchmark$proficient_level`.
The rate is the main measure because it means the same thing in every grade;
a scale score does not. Students without a level that year are counted in `N`
but not in `N_SCORED` or the rate.

The on-time group's counts fall to zero in the later years. In the simulated
data, former ELs leave the panel after their fourth monitoring year
(`sim_contract.md` §3.3), so there is no one left to test. The same section
notes that a real delivery keeps former ELs, so expect the on-time group to
stay in view in your data. The table shows a zero there, not a suppressed
cell.

### `$trajectories`: ELP levels, split by exit group

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Mean reported ELP level by year in status, one line per exit group (simulated data). There is no pooled cohort line, by design."
plot_trajectories(res$trajectories$levels, spec)
```

`$trajectories$levels` holds `EXIT_GROUP`, `YEAR_IN_STATUS`, `N`,
`MEAN_LEVEL`, `MEDIAN_LEVEL` and `SUPPRESSED`. Use
`plot_trajectories(..., measure = "median")` for medians. The on-time line
stops when its students exit, because former ELs take no ELP test.

`$trajectories$composition` shows who is still being tested each year. Its
`PCT_OF_MEASURED` column is each group's share of the students with a score:

```{r}
ft_check2_composition(res)
```

Here the on-time group is `r pct(ot_first)` of the students tested in year 1
and none of them by year `r ot_gone`. That is why the package never draws one
cohort-average line. The plotting function refuses a frame without the group
column:

```{r}
no_groups <- res$trajectories$levels[c("YEAR_IN_STATUS", "MEAN_LEVEL")]
tryCatch(plot_trajectories(no_groups), error = conditionMessage)
```

### `$meta`

`$meta` carries what the report's captions need. The Sample statement, the
cohort, its size and the on-time text are all here:

```{r}
str(res$meta[c("cohort", "cohort_n", "on_time_text", "on_time_provisional",
               "academic_subject", "type_gate_applies")])
```

`on_time_provisional` is `TRUE` when `policy$timelines$source` is
`"provisional"`. The Sample statement then flags the timeline
`[DERIVED — VERIFY]`. `band_clock_note` is `NA` unless the on-time rule
varies by initial band (see Pitfalls). `blocked_note` explains an empty
Additional check.

## How to read it

**Start with the first two rows.** They give the balance of the cohort. Here
`r num(tot[["EXIT_ONTIME"]])` of `r num(tot[["ALL"]])` students exited on time
(`r pct(tot[["EXIT_ONTIME"]] / tot[["ALL"]])`), and `r num(prolonged_n)` are
prolonged: `r num(late_n)` late exiters plus `r num(tot[["NO_EXIT"]])` not
observed to exit by `r panel_last`. Check the identity: `EXIT_EVER` + `NO_EXIT` + `DISAPPEARED`
= All. These numbers illustrate the machinery, nothing more.

**Then read each block down and across.** Read down a column to see what a
group is made of. Read across a row to see how groups differ. The crosstab has
no Prolonged column. For the sharpest contrast, compare `EXIT_ONTIME` with
`NO_EXIT`. A characteristic over-represented among prolonged students is a
candidate explanation for why they are still classified. One spread evenly
across the groups is not. For example, special education students are
`r pct(iep_pct[["EXIT_ONTIME"]])` of on-time exiters and
`r pct(iep_pct[["NO_EXIT"]])` of the students not observed to exit in this
simulated cohort. In real data, a gap like that would raise a question for the
recommendation: a threshold change would not reach those students. Here, the
generator built it in.

**Ask whether the on-time group is already academically stronger.** In year
`r y_first` (mostly grade `r grade_first`), `r pct(ac_pct[["on_time"]])` of
on-time exiters and `r pct(ac_pct[["prolonged"]])` of prolonged students are
proficient in `r res$meta$academic_subject` in the simulated data. Some gap is
built into the definitions: on-time exiters cleared an English bar, and the
content test is in English. The useful question is whether the gap is larger
than that explains, and whether it persists at similar ELP levels. The
trajectory figure lets you check the ELP side.

**Read each trajectory line on its own.** A line shows how the students in
that group scored while they were still classified. A pooled average falls
for two reasons it cannot separate: students growing less, and the fastest
growers leaving. The composition table shows the second. The same effect
works inside the prolonged line: its late exiters stop testing once they
exit, so its later years increasingly describe students who never exited.

**This is not automatically about the cut score.** Findings here concern how
policies, programs, population and exit criteria interact. The right response
may be a program or support change, not a threshold change.

## Pitfalls

- **Never fold Disappeared students into either group.** Censored is not
  did-not-exit. They have their own column and their own `EXIT_GROUP` value.
  The simulated cohort has none; yours probably will.
- **Do not average time to exit.** `$flags` carries `EXIT_YEAR_IN_STATUS`,
  and its mean is tempting. Censoring biases it: the students still classified
  have no exit year to average. Use Check 1's median years to exit and its
  share exited within the timeline instead.
- **The window is finite.** `NO_EXIT` means "not observed exiting by
  `r panel_last`", not "will never exit". `EXIT_MAX` and `EXIT_ONTIME` count
  against the years available. Say so in every caption you write.
- **Nested columns do not add.** Only Ever + No_Exit + Disappeared sums to
  All.
- **Mind the denominators.** Distribution blocks use the column total;
  indicator rows use students with a reported value. `N_BASE` tells you which.
- **Suppressed cells stay `NA`.** Do not back them out by subtraction. Never
  lower `min_cell` or pool cohorts or grades to make cells appear. If you
  derive a new share (for example a Prolonged column from `N`), run
  `apply_suppression()` on it before you report it.
- **Description, not cause.** A crosstab shows one characteristic at a time.
  Two that travel together, such as district size and program model, cannot
  be told apart here. The model that would separate them is not built.
- **Never plot a cohort-average ELP line over time without splitting by exit
  group.** The fastest growers leave, so the average of whoever remains drifts
  down even if no student slows.
- **One kindergarten cohort is the best case.** Do not read it as the state's
  overall exit picture. Later entrants, including newcomers in upper grades,
  are not in it.
- **An on-time rule keyed by initial band changes the Initial ELP block.** If
  `on_time_rule$by_initial_band` is set, each band has its own deadline, and
  `EXIT_ONTIME` down that block restates the policy rather than describing
  students. `res$meta$band_clock_note` then carries the deadlines, and the
  report shows it as a warning. Read `EXIT_MAX`, which uses one window for
  everyone, down that block instead. Such a rule also reads the roster's
  delivered `INITIAL_ELP`, while the crosstab bands the first annual score.
  The two can disagree for a student, which the build notes record as an open
  issue.
- **Watch for circularity under a Type 3 rule.** If the exit rule itself
  includes an academic criterion, the groups are partly defined by the score
  the academic summary compares. The package does not flag this on its own
  yet.
- **Simulated gaps are parameters.** Every group difference in the simulated
  data was set by the generator. None is a finding.
- **The results object is not shareable.** `$flags` and `$profile` are one
  row per student. Keep a saved `res` out of any folder you send to others.

## Decide before moving on

- **Do specific subgroups need separate treatment in Checks 3 and 4?** A
  group heavily over-represented among prolonged students may need its own
  analysis there, rather than being averaged into the whole.
- **What equity considerations must the final recommendation address
  explicitly?** In particular, note any characteristic that separates the
  prolonged group but that a threshold change would leave untouched.

Record both answers. Checks 3 and 4 and the final recommendation draw on
them.

## Additional checks for multi-criterion exit rules

Some states exit students on more than one criterion: a composite plus a
domain floor, or a profile across domains. The package names six exit-rule
types (Types 2–6 have more than one criterion). For these, Check 2 adds the
students **blocked by exactly one criterion** as extra comparison rows. If
such a group looks systematically different from the cohort, that criterion is
screening on something other than what the main score screens on.

The spec declares the type. Check it like this:

```{r}
spec_exit_types(spec)
el_exit_typology()[as.character(spec_exit_types(spec))]
spec_has_type(spec, 2:6)
is.null(res$blocked_groups)
```

The simulated spec is Type 1, a single overall composite, so
`$blocked_groups` is `NULL`. `res$meta$blocked_note` says why:

> `r res$meta$blocked_note`

For a Type 2–6 spec, the slot holds `BLOCKED_BY`, `COLUMN`, `N`, `N_BASE`,
`PCT` and `SUPPRESSED`. `PCT` is the group's share of each exit column. The
groups come from Prep 2's `compute_criteria_crosswalk()`, so the two stages
agree on who is blocked by what. A student blocked by different criteria in
different years is counted under the one that blocked them most often. Show
the table with:

```{r}
#| eval: false
ft_check2_blocked_groups(res)
```

A multi-criterion spec can still come back `NULL` if no cohort student is
blocked by exactly one criterion. `res$meta$type_gate_applies` tells the two
cases apart, and `blocked_note` words each one.

## Render the stage report

The stage report carries the authored walkthrough, every table and figure
above, and the Decide box. Render it with:

```{r}
#| eval: false
render_step("check2")                    # reports/check2_flows.docx and .html
render_step("check2", formats = "html")  # HTML only
```

`render_step()` scans the output for student IDs and stops if it finds any.
The example report on the simulated data is
[on the project site](../check2_flows.html).

The report builds its own results from the simulated data. For your state,
compute the results yourself, then render from the saved file. Pass full
paths: the report renders in a temporary folder.

```{r}
#| eval: false
res <- run_check2(bundle, spec)                    # your bundle and spec
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)        # not a shared folder
saveRDS(res, "results/check2_results.rds")
files <- render_step(
  "check2",
  spec_file    = normalizePath("specs/XX_EL_Spec.R", winslash = "/"),
  results_file = "results/check2_results.rds",
  check_disclosure = FALSE
)
check_output_disclosure(files, bundle)             # scan against your IDs
```

Turn the automatic scan off with `check_disclosure = FALSE`: it can only build
the simulated bundle, so it would check your report against the wrong IDs.
`check_output_disclosure()` then checks the files against every `STUDENT_ID`
in your bundle, and stops if any appears.

Run `render_step()` from a project folder that has no `R/` subfolder. The
report treats a working folder with an `R/` subfolder as the package's source
and tries to load it with `devtools::load_all()`.
